title: BBOWP-Bench: Evaluating LLMs on Black-Box Optimization Word Problems
abstract: arXiv:2608.02612v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Formulating an optimization problem strongly affects final solution quality, yet good formulations usually require substantial expertise. Recent studies have explored automatically deriving optimization problems from natural-language descriptions, but existing benchmarks focus on settings where objectives and constraints can be written explicitly as mathematical expressions. Many practically important problems are naturally treated as black-box optimization (BBO) problems, in which only objective values are observable, and the functional form is unavailable. In BBO, search space design (as part of problem formulation) and optimization algorithm selection are crucial for problem-solving. Automating these processes with large language models (LLMs) remains challenging. translated_title: BBOWP-Bench：评估大语言模型在黑箱优化文字问题上的能力
translated_abstract: 优化问题的建模方式会强烈影响最终解的质量，然而良好的建模通常需要大量专业知识。近期研究已探索从自然语言描述中自动推导优化问题，但现有基准主要针对目标与约束能够显式写成数学表达式的场景。许多实际重要的问题天然适合被视为黑箱优化（BBO）问题——其中只有目标函数值可观测，而函数形式不可获得。在BBO中，搜索空间设计（作为问题建模的一部分）与优化算法的选择对求解至关重要，而利用大语言模型（LLM）自动化这些过程仍具挑战性。我们提出了黑箱优化文字问题，这是一个新颖的问题设定：系统需要从自然语言描述的问题中同时推断出搜索空间并选择优化算法。
tldr: 该论文提出BBOWP-Bench基准，首次评估大语言模型能否从自然语言描述的黑箱优化文字问题中同时推断出合适的搜索空间并选择恰当的优化算法。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces BBOWP-Bench, a benchmark that evaluates whether LLMs can infer both a suitable search space and an appropriate optimization algorithm from natural-language black-box optimization word problems.
